content: Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.
It's not what happens to you, but how you react to it that matters.
It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a lot of it.
attribution: Seneca, On the Shortness of Life

content: The beginning is the most important part of the work.
All men by nature desire to know.

attribution: Rene Descartes, Discourse on the Method

content: It does not matter how slowly you go as long as you do not stop.
A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
The only true wisdom is in knowing you know nothing.
Stoicism is a school of ancient Greek philosophy that teaches the practice of virtue as the only true good, and encourages focusing only on what lies within one's own control.
Existentialism explores questions about individual freedom, choice, and meaning, arguing that people must create their own purpose in a universe that does not provide one automatically.
The Socratic method uses a series of questions and answers to expose contradictions in a person's beliefs, encouraging deeper critical thinking rather than simply providing answers.
The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
Every new beginning comes from some other beginning's end.
Utilitarianism holds that the right action is the one that produces the greatest good for the greatest number of people, judging morality by outcomes rather than intentions.
